parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the national framework is the dominant traveller exposure. Passport sex-marker restrictions are in force, and entry officers are instructed to refuse discrepant or doubtful applicants, with a lifetime fraud finding possible but not automatic. Immigration custody harms are documented, and national hostility includes counterterrorism framing and hospital subpoenas. The division adds a school and college facility rule with no penalty and no enforcement mechanism, a school outing mandate, an unresolved under-18 care and sports ban, and no statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination law. Mitigators are marriage recognition, a federal appellate ruling treating transgender-status discrimination as sex discrimination, and local ordinances. No visitor-facing arrest or street-violence record is documented for this division. Score sits in the high-to-elevated band.

entry_documents.exposure: National cable directs refusal where documents or other evidence cast reasonable doubt on sex, with a case-note tag applied to refused or pending cases. Passport marker restrictions were allowed to take effect in November 2025, and some trans travellers have had passports confiscated or blocked and been stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Lifetime fraud ineligibility is not automatic and requires four elements, with limited waiver options. A civil-liberties suit is pending, and the policy is contested.
entry_documents.interaction: A home-passport mismatch at entry can move into refusal, stranding, or referral to the fraud ground. The division's birth-certificate and licence rules do not change the visitor's entry documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody harms are documented, including forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. Discrepancy-driven detention at the border can lead into this custody. Corrections policy adopted from 2026 and the end of prisoner-count reporting are also documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Judicial challenges are pending. No operative protective custody rule for trans visitors is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border refusal or secondary detention can lead directly into federal immigration custody. The division has no custody authority of its own in the dossier.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: The division's Protect All Students Act requires birth-sex facility designation at K-12 schools, colleges and universities, public and private, and requires students to use facilities matching their birth certificate. Overnight accommodations are included. It has no criminal penalty and no enforcement mechanism, and no arrest or case under it is documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Single-occupancy restrooms with controlled use are exempt. No statewide public-accommodation protection exists for trans visitors in ordinary facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Exposure falls mainly on students and institutions. Visitor adults are not documented as covered by public-building rules here. National facility rules apply to other states and are not attributed to this division.

care_services.exposure: The Saving Adolescents from Experimentation Act bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for under-18s, but its operative status is unresolved after a 2025 re-injunction. Nationally, hospital records of under-19 patients were subpoenaed, and a proposed rule would bar public reimbursement for under-18 care. Adult-care rules were withdrawn in February 2024.
care_services.protection: No documented operative protection for visitors seeking care. Adult care is not restricted under current in-force rules.
care_services.interaction: A minor seeking care can face a provider felony risk, records demands, and a family investigation. Adult care access is not shown to be restricted.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National official framing includes a counterterrorism strategy naming radically pro-transgender groups, cash rewards for leadership identification, and a national directive to prosecute teachers facilitating social transition. The division's house bill from January 2025 requires school staff to out LGBTQ students and removes gender-ideology content from the early grades.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The national strategy disclaims use against people who merely disagree. Some national orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing can reach visitors through border and security channels. The division's outing duty applies to visiting students, not adults.

minors_guardians.exposure: A visiting minor in K-12 or college faces birth-certificate facility designation with no enforcement mechanism. The January 2025 school outing mandate can disclose a student's LGBTQ status to parents. An under-18 care or sports ban may apply if unresolved. A travelling guardian may face school-driven disclosure or care-related records demands.
minors_guardians.protection: Parental opt-out applies only to the curriculum component. No documented school complaint procedure is sourced.
minors_guardians.interaction: School designation and outing can separate care from the travelling child and create state inquiry for a guardian. Care restrictions can compound these risks.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific street violence rate or visitor-targeted incident is documented for this division. National hate-crime coverage exists, but 37 states lacked gender-identity bias statutes as of 2019. Division-level coverage is not stated.
street_violence_police_response.protection: A national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity. Thirty-three localities bar gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse depends on local ordinances and national federal statutes. Statewide protection is absent from the dossier.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination statute for private employment, housing or public accommodations. Trans candidates were disqualified in 2024. The August 2026 marker rules are announced but unverified. County refusals of birth-certificate corrections continue.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Marriage recognition for any spouses, a federal appellate ruling on sex discrimination, and a state executive order covering state employment. Birth-certificate corrections are permitted since 2021 in most counties.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local ordinances cover some visitors in some cities. Statewide remedies are thin. Court challenges to the national and division measures are unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: The anchor features birth-sex shelter admission, police raids with bribe-based release, and institutional exclusion. This dossier documents no raids, bribes or criminal arrests of visitors in the division. Its custody harms are national immigration custody, not the division's own. It is therefore higher than 0.25-E, though still carries national custody exposure.

The anchor features routine, discretionary exclusion of visibly trans visitors, with near-unreachable appeals. This dossier shows passport-based refusal and stranding and a fraud-ground risk, but the screening is case-based and not universal. The division adds no exclusion register. The dossier is close to 0.35-A on entry, with less exposure in the division itself.

The anchor has statewide protections, police powers against harassment, and an independent review board with enforcement. This dossier lacks statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination law and documents national enforcement-type hostility. The gap is large, so the case sits well below 0.75-D.

The anchor has statutory protections in all public conveyances, trained police and enforced complaints. This dossier has no statewide protection and documented entry refusal and facility exposure, so it is far below 0.95-B.

parsed.synthesis: The operative exposure is a combination. National entry screening can refuse or strand a visitor whose documents mismatch presentation, and refusal can lead into federal immigration custody where harm is documented. National official framing and hospital records demands add to the pressure. The division's own facility rule for schools and colleges has no penalty and no documented case, so its direct adult-visitor effect is small. Its outing mandate and unresolved under-18 care and sports bans matter mainly for minors and guardians. Local ordinances and marriage recognition provide only partial recourse. Because the division has no statewide gender-identity protection and no documented enforcement against visitors, the rating stays in the high-to-elevated band.
